results.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R2-1.test.ts`. The test calls createGame(root), focuses the start screen's primary RACE button, and dispatches cancelable Space keydown and keyup events that bubble. It fails at `expect(down.defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` (received true): keyboard.ts:52-57 calls preventDefault on every Space keydown on window, and :64 does the same for the matching keyup. game.ts creates the input once with no mode or pause gating.
results.reason: A browser activates a focused button on Space through the keydown/keyup default action. That default is now cancelled on every screen, so Space no longer presses RACE, RESUME or NEXT RACE. On main, Space was not handled at all.

results.trace: Ran the test. It starts Dust Bowl (seed 1, PLAYER_CAR_COUNT) and plays bot inputs from a twin world until racers[0].armed is true. Then it sends Esc (paused true), Space keydown and keyup on window, and Esc again (paused false), then runs 3 frames. It fails at `expect(boostTicks).toBe(0)`, received 88. The tap latched actionTapped while paused (keyboard.ts:55), and setPaused's resume branch (game.ts:171-173) never calls input.reset(), so the first input.read() after resume carries action: true.
results.reason: A Space press made on the pause screen fires the boost right after resume. Resetting the input on resume fixes it.

results.trace: grep for decodeInputs/replayInputs in src: the only consumers are replay.ts:134 (length validation) and runReplay at :147, which passes frames straight to stepWorld. stepWorld reads input.action, and the non-enumerable property returns true. pickup-replay.test.ts already proves runReplay matches the live run.
results.reason: No code in the repo spreads, serialises or clones decoded frames, so the claimed divergence is hypothetical. The non-enumerable property meets AC6 while keeping the existing append-only test replay.test.ts:63 passing, and the proposed API change goes beyond the spec.

results.trace: Ran the test: createRaceUi, reset, then sync the same pickup RaceView (pickups:[true], racers with armed:false and boostTicks:0) twice, with a MutationObserver on document.body during the second sync. Two mutation records come back, both targeting 'ui-panel ui-panel--navy ui-keys__panel'. They come from keycap-legend.ts:63-65, where setPowerUp(true) calls panel.insertBefore(powerUp, pause) unguarded on every sync (race-ui.ts:151).
results.reason: On pickup tracks every frame removes and re-inserts the POWER-UP node, which breaks the 'unchanged frame touches no DOM' contract that race-ui.test.ts enforces for other tracks.

results.trace: pickups.stage.ts:11 calls raceStage(root,{...racers, at: AT}). raceStage (stage.ts:113-116) builds the view {phase,countdown,raceTick,racers}, computes cars with o.at.map(a => carOnTrack(track.centre,a)) and syncs. pickups.stage.ts:13-14 then calls stageTrack() again, rebuilds the same view literal with pickups added, recomputes the same cars with AT.map(a => carOnTrack(centre,a)) and syncs a second time. RaceStageOptions (stage.ts:86-97) has no pickups field, which is why the stage copies the code. The first sync runs legend.setPowerUp(false) and touch.setAction on the same racers, so the stage passes through a state with no POWER-UP keycap.
results.reason: The stage re-implements raceStage's view and car building only to add `pickups`. An optional pickups option on RaceStageOptions does the same job without the copy or the double sync.

results.trace: Same root cause and location as R2-4 (keycap-legend.ts setPowerUp re-inserting on every sync).

world.ts:152-153 sets r.armed = i===0 && p.armed and r.boostTicks = i===0 ? p.boostTicks : 0. Tests: pickups.test.ts:104-123 (the only one asserting armed false on AI racers) steers the player off into the infield and parks it (offTrack, then NO_INPUT), so p.armed stays false and `r.armed` would be false even after the mutation `r.armed = p.armed`. pickups.test.ts:79-101 (carCount 2) and pickup-replay.test.ts:37-56 (carCount 3) only read racers[0]. pickups.test.ts:164 strips armed and boostTicks before comparing. boost.test.ts:18 uses carCount 1. No test asserts AI racer views while the player is armed or boosting.
results.reason: AC2's 'AI racer views always show armed false' is never checked in the one situation where it can fail, so leaking the player's state into AI views would pass every test.

results.trace: pickups.test.ts:66-69 only asserts Math.hypot(p.x-cx, p.z-cz) < |lateral|+1.5. If track.ts:382 returned {x:p.x, z:p.z} (lateral dropped), the distance would be about 0 < 3.5+1.5 and the test would pass. Flipping the sign of lateral gives the same distance and would pass too. No other test checks the lateral offset against an independent expectation: pickups-scene.test.ts compares meshes with trackLayout's own output.
results.reason: AC1's 'one world {x,z} per pickup' is not pinned down. Collapsed or mirrored lateral offsets would pass every test.

results.trace: touch-controls.css:35-40 places .ui-touch__slot--action at right: safe-right + (touch-gas - touch-action)/2 and bottom: safe-bottom + touch-gas + space-s3, which is centred above GAS. action-button.test.ts proves the button exists inside .ui-touch and the stage renders it.
results.reason: The layout is correct today. It is purely visual, the screenshots and the registered stage cover it, and CLAUDE.md asks visual features only for a test that proves the element exists. A coverage nicety, not a defect.

results.trace: action-button.test.ts AC8 asserts only `b?.querySelector('svg polygon')).not.toBeNull()`. icons.ts:7-19 draws every icon (play, pause, restart, arrows, home, keys) from polygons, so replacing icon('bolt',…) with icon('play',…) at touch-controls.ts:41 would still pass. Only 'bolt' has the points '14,2 4,14 11,14 9,22 20,9 13,9'.
results.reason: AC8 explicitly requires the lightning icon, and the test that claims to check it accepts any icon.
